ctx.x: Famous Door on 52nd Street. Actually the location was just off of 52nd Street. It was on 7th Avenue right across from what’s now the Sheridan Hotel. It’s a big office building or something now but in those days, in the basement there was a huge room, which they called this Famous Door. The Famous Door had actually been on 52nd Street but they called this one the Famous Door and the show included Pearl Bailey as a headliner, and Eddie South and the big band, a guy named Jimmy Smith who tapped dance on a…

and so I knew how he played, but he always had like a six piece group with Jonah Jones or somebody like that and funny… they did a lot of comedy but they played good music. One thing that people don’t understand with those groups like Stuff Smith, and Louie Jordan, and the Three Flames and some of those other groups, Nat Cole even in those days, they did a lot of humorous material. They played some funny things, things that made you laugh but they played great. It was always in the context of very good jazz. I…

items.title: 68728_Jonah
items.q: I'm going over to the Downbeat with Billy Taylor.

ctx.x: Would Bushkin give Mingus any time to play or anything?

I don't think he gave him enough. I don't think he gave him enough, because Mingus one day Mingus come in and he put in his notice and he said, "I'm going over to the Downbeat with Billy Taylor." And so Bushkin had to find a bass player. So I tell Bushkin about I've got a man for him. Nobody knew him around here at that time, Milt Hinton. I said, "I've got a man named Milt Hinton." You notice you never heard him play anything till he got out of Cab's band. Well, I'm the one that got him started with Bushkin. He…

He said, "I come by the band and heard him when he was in Birdland. I didn't hear too much." I said, "Look, this guy's a good bass player. He can play any way. He can play -- he can play just with the left hand, and all that stuff," and that's what Joe liked. He liked the bass player to play the same things in his left hand. So he was a little reluctant about it, so I said, "Well, look try him. Tell him to come down one night. I'll tell him to come down one night, and that's it, you know." So he said, "Okay."…
